races.name: Sky Bet "Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe" Handicap Stakes (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Kodiac Thriller
runners_data.note: Front-runner by nature but steps back from 6f to 5f where he won last time out; visor applied, trainer Mark Walford in fair recent form (3/14), and Good to Firm conditions replicate that win exactly — a genuine pace-pressing threat.

runners_data.name: Lethal Nymph
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and the key pace influence in this race; Paul Midgley handler in modest nick (1/11 over 14 days) but the horse's ability to lead unchallenged is what matters most, and her 5f Good to Firm form (2nd, 4th) shows she handles these conditions.

runners_data.name: Almaty Star
runners_data.note: True hold-up operator for Robert Cowell who needs others to force the pace; won at 5f Good to Firm and placed on Tapeta in similar style, so conditions suit, but a slow tempo set by a lone leader is the worst-case scenario for her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Emerald Harmony
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with an excellent profile on 5f Good to Firm ground (1W6P in 11 qualifying runs), trained by Paul Midgley who has two runners here; Jonathan England gets the ride and this horse's natural position tracking the pace makes it ideally placed in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Roberto Caro
runners_data.note: Holds-up and has headgear (tongue-tie) applied; his 5f trip record is light and the Going to Firm conditions are a step up from his preferred easier surface — a hold-up horse who needs more pace than Lethal Nymph alone may generate.

runners_data.name: King's Call
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher at the wrong end of the form card — five consecutive placings of 10th or worse on Good and Good to Firm ground suggest he is not firing, and the ⚠ fade flag reinforces that he is unlikely to be a factor regardless of pace shape.

runners_data.name: Mon Na Slieve
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes, a top jump jockey, takes the mount for Kevin Ryan; a genuine hold-up horse on 5f Good to Firm ground with 11 qualifying runs (1W2P), she needs a true end-to-end gallop to deliver her best and may find the tempo too sedate.

runners_data.name: Sports Coach
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent for Antony Brittain and has placed at 5f on similar surfaces (2nd at Southwell); Sean Quinlan rides and the horse's ability to race off a fast pace makes it relevant if Kodiac Thriller or others push the early fractions harder behind Lethal Nymph.

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends this horse out 19 days fresh with tongue-tie and cheekpieces; his hold-up style has produced two wins at 5f Good to Firm but his last six form figures show inconsistency and Dylan Johnston is not a natural flat rider — treat with caution.

runners_data.name: Managing Director
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in character — winner at 5f Good to Firm — but the overcrowded hold-up division means he is mapped to midfield and effectively racing away from his natural territory; Danny McMenamin rides and the form profile (1W3P in six qualifying runs) is strong if he can find daylight.

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon-trained 4-year-old with solid placed form (0W3P) at 5f Good to Firm; his true hold-up style is compromised by the field's overall makeup, and Kevin Brogan's jump background means he may struggle to place this horse tactically in a fast-moving flat sprint.

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls runner with a healthy 5f Good to Firm record (2W3P in 12 qualifying runs); a natural hold-up horse who finds himself in a congested midfield through redistribution — Brendan Powell rides and if he threads through he is capable, but the scenario requires things to go right.

runners_data.name: Ventura Express
runners_data.note: Veteran 9-year-old for Paul Midgley (trainer's third runner) who has placed nine times at 5f Good to Firm without a win in recent attempts; his hold-up style is negated by the pack's depth, and Tristan Durrell faces a tough task getting him competitive.

runners_data.name: Cameley Days
runners_data.note: Won at 5f Good to Firm and placed four times, so conditions clearly suit this 4-year-old; runs in headgear (cheekpieces) and while James Best has experience, the horse's deeper-than-natural position in the field (true hold-up type) makes a challenge from the rear harder to execute in a moderately-run race.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's 7-year-old won at 5f Good to Firm and has placed twice in qualifying conditions; Harry Reed takes the ride with 14 days' turnaround — compact enough — but the horse's genuine hold-up style is buried in a crowded middle section and a slow tempo works directly against him.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby has an excellent 5f Good to Firm record through this horse (3W6P in 12 runs) and Dream Deal returns just five days after its last run with a tongue-tie and breast girth; the real style is hold-up but Richie McLernon must navigate 17 runners from a deep position in a race not run to suit.

runners_data.name: Bayraat
runners_data.note: Tom Tate's 10-year-old has an exceptional placed record (1W7P) at 6f Good to Firm but now drops to 5f — a trip he has tried only once recently; Caoilin Quinn rides and his naturally prominent style could see him feature if the fractions are kind, though the trip-drop is a concern.

races.paceDynamic: Lethal Nymph is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — she will stride out from the gates and control fractions on Good to Firm ground at York's straight five furlongs without being pressured into a suicidal gallop. With Kodiac Thriller, Emerald Harmony, Sports Coach and Bayraat all naturally prominent types, a battle for early position will ignite behind her, but none is likely to seriously contest her for the rail and the lead itself. The result is a race run at a sustainable, front-runner-friendly tempo rather than a true end-to-end gallop, which compresses the finishing straight and reduces the opportunity for hold-up horses to reel in the leader. This shape strongly favours runners racing prominently or just off the pace — horses tracking Lethal Nymph in positions two through four — because they receive the clearest run on fast ground and are never asked to find an impossible closing burst; the redistribution of Managing Director, Cayman Tai, Tees Aggregates, Ventura Express, Cameley Days, Harb and Dream Deal into midfield underlines that the true hold-up contingent is overcrowded and unable to secure natural rear positions, so most will be further forward than ideal and competing for the same ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lethal Nymph Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Lethal Nymph leads unchallenged and sets a comfortable, controlled tempo that plays into the hands of horses tracking just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Lethal Nymph dictates from the front without serious pressure, and a prominent chaser who has tracked the pace travels into the race with cover before asserting in the final furlong on ground that suits quick-finishing types; the steady fractions mean stamina reserves are intact for those who raced within themselves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the sustainable pace set by Lethal Nymph is never seriously tested and she conserves enough energy to hold on all the way to the line.
scenarios.body: Lethal Nymph, granted a soft lead with no rival willing to commit early, dictates every yard and finds reserves in the final furlong that a lone front-runner on Good to Firm ground at York's five furlongs can genuinely produce; the hold-up horses fail to generate the momentum needed to close in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly fast early pace — driven by prominent types scrambling for position — burns off the leaders and leaves a gap for closers to exploit.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop for positions two and three behind Lethal Nymph raises the tempo enough to leave the front-runners vulnerable in the final 100 yards, allowing any genuine hold-up runner that gets a clean passage to finish strongly; however, the redistribution of most true hold-up horses into already-crowded midfield makes a clean run hard to find and this scenario is materially less likely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Draw, Wider Draw Wins
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems and positional chaos across 17 runners on the straight five furlongs result in an unexpected winner emerging from an unfavoured part of the field.
scenarios.body: The sheer volume of runners creates a wall of horses across the track, and any prominent-type drawn wide who finds a clean passage benefits from the mayhem while those drawn awkwardly are trapped without room; this is the least predictable shape but the wide-draw angle is a genuine consideration in large-field five-furlong handicaps at York.

watchPoints.text: Lethal Nymph leads unchallenged — if she clears the gate cleanly and hits the front by a length inside the first furlong, the race shape is locked in and prominent trackers like Emerald Harmony become the primary danger.

With 17 runners across a straight 5f, watch the draw and early positioning battle among Kodiac Thriller, Sports Coach and Emerald Harmony — if two or more commit to chasing Lethal Nymph aggressively, the pace lifts enough to bring closers into play.

Managing Director, Cayman Tai and Tees Aggregates are all genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield — if any secures an unexpected clear passage wider than drawn, they each carry form good enough to finish fast on this ground.

Dream Deal runs just five days after its last outing for Tim Easterby — the trainer's short-turnaround runners are worth tracking in large-field sprint handicaps, and this horse's 5f Good to Firm strike rate (3W6P) is the best in the field on that surface/trip combination.

King's Call has finished 10th or worse in five consecutive starts on Good and Good to Firm ground and carries the ⚠ fade flag — any opening drift in the market should be treated as a genuine signal to look elsewhere.

races.name: Sky Bet Dash (Class 2 Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Pocklington
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Geoff Oldroyd; won over this C&D on Standard and is the race's lone genuine pace-setter, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) notes she is technically racing out of her natural P role — she sets the pace here and Good to Firm is fine, but recent form (12784) is patchy and she carries the burden of 22 runners behind her.

runners_data.name: Stratusnine
runners_data.note: James Doyle booking for Hugo Palmer adds instant class; travels prominently and has five placings from 14 runs on Good, including a recent second over 6f on this going — well-handicapped if producing his best and the mile trip form suggests he stays every yard of the 6f.

runners_data.name: Addison Grey
runners_data.note: Clive Cox has a strong 4/28 14-day strike-rate and Rossa Ryan is a confident booking; nine runs on Good going producing two wins and six places is an outstanding surface record, and all five recent runs have been over 6f on Good — ideally suited to these conditions.

runners_data.name: Apollo One
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the mount on this hold-up type who needs things to go wrong for the prominent horses; 8-year-old has genuine ability (OR 94) but recent form reads poorly (829390) and late ground at York over 6f is a real ask in a race likely to be run at an even tempo.

runners_data.name: Commanche Falls
runners_data.note: Michael Dods runner ran just 8 days ago which bears monitoring for residual fatigue; has placed four times from 11 Good-ground runs at OR 94 and likes to be handy — headgear (p) helps him concentrate, and a clean draw is important at York in a 22-runner field.

runners_data.name: Coul Angel
runners_data.note: Four places from eight Good-ground runs gives Michael Appleby's 4-year-old solid surface credentials; tends to race prominently but with so many natural P horses in the field he may find himself a length or two further back than ideal, though Clifford Lee is capable of manufacturing a run.

runners_data.name: Air Force One
runners_data.note: Geoff Oldroyd's second runner wears a visor and has two wins on Good to Firm over 5f — the step to 6f is the key question as all five recent runs are over the minimum trip; if he gets a prominent berth he stays well enough at this level but P J McDonald will need to manage him into the race carefully.

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: Ran just 5 days ago for David O'Meara, which is sharp but the trainer's 5/43 14-day rate means horses are fit and ready; won over 6f on Good (1/6f/GOO in hist) and placed twice more — Kieran Shoemark has the experience to slot into a clean position in this crowded field.

runners_data.name: Novello Lad
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's 5-year-old has won his last two starts (6f Good, 6f Soft) and carries top recent form into this race; Paul Mulrennan is a proven big-field handler and 13 runs on Good ground producing three wins makes this the best surface form in the field — a key player if he can hold his prominent berth.

runners_data.name: Musical Touch
runners_data.note: Fahey's 5-year-old has won at 6f on Good and on Standard — genuine surface form exists — but the key context is that he is a natural prominent racer squeezed into a midfield position on this map because the forward slots are oversubscribed; Warren Fentiman (3) is a 3lb claimer which helps offset the weight, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects the competitive pressure for early position.

runners_data.name: Red Spells Danger
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 3-year-old has two wins and two seconds from five 6f runs on Good — the best recent form profile in the race; OR 93 on just 126lbs is potentially well-treated by the weights and David Allan knows Easterby's runners intimately, making this one of the most prominent contenders for the lead group.

runners_data.name: We Never Stop
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's hold-up type has only one recent place (2/6f/GOO) across 15 Good-ground runs and has run poorly recently (938002); Kevin Stott is capable but this horse needs a stronger pace than is expected here to close effectively, and the 0W from 15 similar-going runs is a concern.

runners_data.name: Trilby
runners_data.note: Sam England's 6-year-old has won twice over 5f on Soft and placed three times on Good — the Soft wins are a slight flag on today's Good to Firm — but more critically he is a natural prominent racer who, given the overcrowded pace situation, is unlikely to secure his preferred early position; Rowan Scott can improvise but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) correctly flags the risk.

runners_data.name: Rousing Encore
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 6-year-old has a 3/6f/GOO in its recent history and is a genuine prominent type, yet finds himself mapped to midfield by weight of numbers; James Sullivan has ridden him before and 10 Good-ground runs with one place from a prominent berth underlines the importance of position — losing that position materially reduces his chance here.

runners_data.name: Baldomero
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 8-year-old hold-up type runs in a visor and has two recent third-place finishes on Good going but a 0W record from 15 similar-going starts; Toby Moore's 7lb claim helps on the weights (122lbs effectively lower) but this horse needs the pace to collapse for a late run and that is unlikely on current evidence.

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie has a 3/47 14-day rate which is modest, but Lauren Young (5) clips the weight; the horse is a natural prominent runner forced back into midfield by sheer competition for forward berths — three wins on Good going at 5f are the performance ceiling, and stepping to 6f on Good to Firm introduces a distance question.

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 4-year-old wears a visor, ran 7 days ago, and has four career placings on Good going including two seconds over 6f; Mark Winn is a capable claimer but this hold-up horse has a 1W from 15 similar-going runs and needs pace — ran well latest (2/6f/GOO) which is at least encouraging.

runners_data.name: Evening Blues
runners_data.note: Stephen Hanlon's 3-year-old is best known for middle-distance form (8f wins) and the drop to 6f Good to Firm is a significant change of parameters; he is a natural prominent racer being mapped rearward by force of numbers, wears headgear (h) for the first time, and the STYLE_FIT discount (0.91) reflects that he cannot operate on his own terms today.

runners_data.name: Fivethousandtoone
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 8-year-old wears a p and has five runs on Similar going producing no wins — a flat form profile; Duran Fentiman takes the ride on a horse that has front-running inclinations but cannot secure that position in this field, and a 6/6f/GOO recent run suggests modest current form.

runners_data.name: Utmost Respect
runners_data.note: Amie Waugh (3) picks up the ride on this Fahey 3-year-old who has not run for 288 days — a significant absence that creates a major fitness unknown; won over 5f on Good (1/5f/GOO in hist) and showed early promise, but returning from a near-10-month break into a 22-runner heritage handicap is a stiff ask regardless of talent.

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: Fahey's 6-year-old has one win over 6f on Good and is a natural prominent type whose typical race position is congested away by the pace map; Cam Hardie is experienced enough to find cover, and 5 similar-going runs from 15 with one win and three places is respectable, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) signals a genuine positional risk.

races.paceDynamic: Pocklington is the confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, is unlikely to face serious early pressure from a rival prepared to burn past her — she should dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front on Good to Firm ground at York. The field is saturated with natural prominent racers: Red Spells Danger, Commanche Falls, Stratusnine, Addison Grey, Veblen Good, Novello Lad, Coul Angel and Air Force One will all be pressing to sit just off the pace, compressing the field into a tight early bunch and meaning the race is run at a fair, uniform tempo rather than a dawdle or a frenzy. With no horse likely to inject a true scorching pace, the race will settle quickly into a prominent-led procession and the finish will be decided in the final 2f, favouring those who travel sweetly in the first three or four and carry momentum through — hold-up horses will find the gaps late but the clean-paced shape suits prominent types who can organise their run off a predictable gallop. This field contains far more front-running and prominent types than the race can physically accommodate — Musical Touch, Evening Blues, Trilby, Rousing Encore, Eternal Sunshine, Fivethousandtoone, Havana Rum and Rock Opera are all genuine prominent racers who are likely to find themselves racing further back than is natural; those best-placed to actually secure their preferred ground early are Pocklington, Red Spells Danger, Novello Lad and Commanche Falls given their draw, rider experience and recent form at the trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Pocklington sets a fair pace and the compressed midfield group can never quicken past the handiest runners in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Pocklington dictates at a sustainable clip on Good to Firm ground and the horses who travel closest to her — Red Spells Danger, Novello Lad, Addison Grey — get a clean run and arrive with momentum intact; with so many redistributed horses unable to get their natural forward position, the lead group is untroubled and the winner comes from the front four or five.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close-Up Types Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough to string the field but the winner delivers their run from third or fourth rather than on the leader's back.
scenarios.body: The uniform tempo rewards horses who travel smoothly just off the leader without getting into a speed duel early, allowing them to quicken decisively inside the final furlong; Veblen Good and Stratusnine profile well for this scenario given their recent form over the course and distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the front rank ties up inside the final furlong, creating a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Apollo One or We Never Stop, genuine hold-up horses with strong closing profiles on Good ground, would be the chief beneficiaries if the pack of prominent horses burn each other off and leave a clear late lane; this is a lower-probability shape because the pace is not expected to be truly searching and the redistributed horses are not genuine closers who can deliver the required sustained finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If a lower-rated redistributed horse manages to secure a prominent berth against expectations and the race falls unusually truly.
scenarios.body: Rock Opera or Havana Rum have both won over the course and distance at their natural prominent style and if the pace bunches and a pocket of rail room opens, their course form gives them an outside chance; this remains a low-probability scenario given both are racing out of role and carry high STYLE_FIT discounts.

races.name: Sky Bet York Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Royal Champion
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has won this race previously and clearly loves York; his 12 runs on similar going (4W 8P) underscore his credentials on quick ground, and a 90-day absence is the key query, though K.R. Burke's 10/34 fortnight record suggests the yard is in form.|

runners_data.name: Damysus
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden hold a strong hand here — James Doyle partners a horse who has won twice at this trip on good ground and arrives on a reasonable 39-day break; his profile screams progressive type stepping back up to 1m2½f where he won most recently.|

runners_data.name: Dancing Gemini
runners_data.note: The hood (first-time or retained headgear) is worth noting, but five consecutive placed or defeated runs since his sole 2024 win and a form string of 9-4-5-6-5 paint a picture of a horse struggling to reproduce his best; as the only genuine hold-up runner, he needs a stronger pace than this small field is likely to generate.|

runners_data.name: Pride Of Arras
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old is by inclination a front-runner, but with Royal Champion likely to dictate unchallenged he is effectively rerouted off his natural game — his 7/7 record on similar going is strong on paper, but racing against his style in a field with a dominant pace-setter is a tangible negative.|

runners_data.name: Item
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's lightly-raced three-year-old carries the lowest weight (128lbs) and showed plenty winning back-to-back earlier in his career, but his last run — ninth of 12 over this trip on soft — raises a small flag; a natural prominent racer, he too will struggle to get his preferred position with Royal Champion already there and Damysus likely to press.|

races.paceDynamic: Royal Champion is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners over 1m2½f on good-to-firm ground at York, he will set a measured, sustainable tempo without any genuine challenger to his position. Damysus and Item are both natural prominent types who will look to press close behind, while Pride Of Arras — also a true front-runner by inclination — is squeezed into a position further back than he would naturally want given the competition for early ground. This field holds more prominent and front-running types than the race shape can accommodate: Royal Champion is best-placed to secure the lead, with Damysus likely to slot in second, leaving Pride Of Arras and Item unable to fulfil their natural roles and forced wider or deeper than ideal. A controlled, single-file tempo at York's flat mile-and-a-half on quick ground strongly favours horses that can travel prominently in the slipstream and produce a sustained finishing effort — the hold-up operator Dancing Gemini faces the stiffest challenge given the lack of strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Sustained Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Champion dictates an uncontested, even gallop and kicks off the home turn on good-to-firm ground.
scenarios.body: Royal Champion bowls along at his own rhythm, setting just enough pace to stretch the field without burning out, and his closest pursuers Damysus and Item simply cannot find the reserves to overhaul him late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Champion's tempo proves a fraction too slow and a pressing rival produces a decisive move turning for home.
scenarios.body: Damysus, travelling smoothly just off the leader, exploits his superior turn of foot on quick ground and sweeps past in the straight; his 2W from 7 runs on similar going is a strong credential for this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to create a gap for a sustained late run from the back of the small field.
scenarios.body: Dancing Gemini, wearing a hood and operating off a fast pace, would need a stronger gallop than a lone front-runner in a five-horse field typically generates; his recent form figures of 9-4-5-6-5 make this shape a long shot even if the pace obliges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaotic Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Champion sets a false or stop-start gallop and the race implodes into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With no reliable strong tempo, Pride Of Arras — unable to get his natural lead — could produce an unexpected late surge if he has settled better than his race position suggests; this scenario requires multiple things to go wrong simultaneously and is the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Royal Champion jumps and secures the lead cleanly — if Clifford Lee is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, monitor whether he is still travelling comfortably entering the straight, as a comfortable leader here is very hard to peg back over this flat York straight.

Damysus's early positioning is critical: if James Doyle slots in directly behind Royal Champion in second, he is ideally placed for Scenario A or B; if he is shuffled wider or sits third, his chance diminishes.

Pride Of Arras's race begins at the start — watch whether Rossa Ryan attempts to push forward to claim a prominent spot or accepts the hold-up role; forcing the issue against Royal Champion could leave him flat late, while being too passive wastes his best asset.

Dancing Gemini's headgear (hood) is worth tracking in the parade ring and at the start for signs of improved temperament — if he jumps cleanly and settles, his hold-up profile becomes marginally more relevant, though the shallow pace remains a structural problem for him.

With only five runners on a flat, fair track, the draw and early positioning in the first two furlongs will essentially set the final race order — any scrimmaging or traffic issues from the gate could be unusually significant given the lack of tactical flexibility at this trip.

races.name: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Final Night
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed twice at 8f on good ground in recent starts; Connor Beasley takes the mount for John Butler, who is 4 from 10 in the last 14 days, and a mark of 79 on good-to-firm at York looks workable if she sits a handy second or third early.

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: David Allan partners this hold-up type who has been consistently placed at 7f on good ground but steps up to a mile for the first time in this run; the extra furlong is an unknown but his consistent recent form (three placings from five) keeps him relevant if the pace builds.

runners_data.name: Paladin
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, whose recent win at 8f on standard ground (form: 102) shows he can dictate and see it out; operating slightly out of his natural style comfort zone per the STYLE_FIT flag, but with no pace rival to challenge him, Rossa Ryan can dictate his own fractions and that is a significant tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Christian Howarth (3) rides this hold-up horse who has won twice at 8f on good ground and was fourth from further out last time; returning from 31 days off for Scott Dixon, who has been firing (2/14 in 14 days), and a drop back from 10f to 8f suits a horse who stays well.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old is a genuine closer by nature — placed or winning in five of last six — but is tagged as redistributed here, meaning she is unlikely to be as far back as she would ideally want with multiple hold-up horses competing for the same rear-field ground; only 6 days since last run and the tongue tie is noted.

runners_data.name: Cancan In The Rain
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won at 8f on good ground earlier in the season and has run well in defeat since (two fourths); Tom Eaves knows this horse well and the visor is a positive headgear note — ideal profile if the race is run at a fair pace from the front.

runners_data.name: Dwindling Funds
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners this consistent prominent type who has two wins and six placings over 8-9f on good ground; fitted with a hood, and back to his best trip after an unplaced effort at 12f — he will want to press Paladin and ensure the race doesn't become too slowly run.

runners_data.name: Madame De Sevigne
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has struggled to win recently (form: 073879) and her best form figures on similar going show zero wins from eight qualifying runs; the tongue tie is noted but the overall profile makes her hard to trust with confidence here.

runners_data.name: Rajapour
runners_data.note: Recent winner at 8f on good ground (form: 1 from last), fitted with a tongue tie and cheekpieces, running just 6 days after last start; Mark Winn rides and the horse's prominent style and course-relevant going record (1W4P in 8 good-ground runs) make him one of the more interesting prominent-side threats.

runners_data.name: Enola Grey
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose recent form reads five, five, six, six, eight across the board with zero wins and zero places on similar going from five qualifying runs; Kaiya Fraser (amateur) takes the mount for Gemma Tutty and this profile is very hard to recommend in a 17-runner field where getting a run late will be difficult.

runners_data.name: Montezin
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been running exclusively over 6-7f in recent starts and this step up to a mile at York on good-to-firm is an unproven trip on an unproven surface combination; Cam Hardie rides for Antony Brittain, whose yard has been quiet (0/4 in 14 days), and the headgear (hood and cheekpieces) was fitted when he finished eighth last time.

runners_data.name: Bowood
runners_data.note: Elle-May Croot (5) rides this hold-up type who has been placed twice at 8f on good ground but has generally disappointed in recent starts (form: -56573); running six days since last outing and the weight of evidence from his recent going profile (0W2P from 6 qualifying runs) doesn't inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Barry's Boy
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby's mount is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — winner at 8f on standard going and placed at 10f — but is redistributed into midfield here as the map can't place all the closers at the rear; Denis Coakley yard has been quiet (0/4 in 14 days) and the step back in trip from 10f to 8f is a positive.

runners_data.name: Draupnir
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides this four-year-old who has been placed three times from seven runs on good ground, though mostly at 7-9f rather than a flat mile; a true hold-up type by history but placed in midfield on the map through redistribution — if the race produces a genuine test, his staying profile could be a minor factor.

runners_data.name: Up The Jazz
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman (3) partners this genuinely consistent hold-up performer who has placed five times from ten runs on good ground at 8f, including a win; however, as a redistributed closer he may not operate from as far back as suits him, and at OR 70 he is at the bottom of the weights.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old has placed in three of his last five starts at 8f on good ground and, while a natural hold-up type placed into midfield through redistribution, his record of consistent short-margin finishes at this exact trip on this going suggests he will be hitting the line late — if he gets daylight.

runners_data.name: Kiss Me My Love
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who won at 8f on good ground (form: 1) and has been placed five times at this trip on this surface from ten qualifying runs; redistributed from the rear by the map due to overcrowding, Rowan Scott rides and she has the profile of a horse capable of finishing strongly if given a clear passage.

races.paceDynamic: Paladin is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push him on a flat mile at York on good-to-firm ground, he is likely to set a controlled, sustainable tempo from the front. Final Night and Cancan In The Rain will look to sit prominently just behind him, while Dwindling Funds and Rajapour add further cover in the prominent berths, meaning the first three or four furlongs should be orderly rather than frantic. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Financer, Barry's Boy, Draupnir, Up The Jazz, Barley and Kiss Me My Love are all genuine closers who will be competing for ground in the latter stages but are unlikely all to get a clean run off a steady gallop. This race shape — a single uncontested pace-setter, honest but not brutal fractions on a flat, fair track — strongly favours horses racing prominently who can stay close to the tempo and pick off a tiring Paladin in the final two furlongs, rather than pure hold-up horses who need a true end-to-end gallop to get into it late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Paladin Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Paladin bowls along at a fair but unchallenged clip and the prominent chasers track him into the straight with cover.
scenarios.body: Paladin sets fractions comfortable enough to preserve stamina, and the horses immediately behind him — Final Night, Cancan In The Rain, Dwindling Funds — are perfectly placed to pounce inside the final two furlongs; the wide-open flat York straight rewards those who have saved energy by racing close to the pace without chasing it. This is the dominant shape given a lone front-runner on good-to-firm ground over a mile, and it squarely suits horses with a prominent racing style who handle this surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Increases, Hold-Ups Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Paladin is pressed harder than expected by Dwindling Funds or Rajapour, lifting the tempo and causing the pace group to tie up.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested gallop would spread the field and create a genuine stamina test, allowing the hold-up horses who can produce a sustained late run to pick up the pieces in the final furlong. Canvas, who has won twice at this trip on good ground and drops from longer trips, and Kiss Me My Love, most recently third at 8f on good ground, are the profile types who could benefit — though several redistribution-tagged runners in this slot will not truly be operating from far enough back to deliver that finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Falters, Sole Front-Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Paladin's controlled fractions are even steadier than anticipated and the race turns into a sprint finish from two out.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run affair off a very slow gallop can sometimes deliver the front-runner a clear advantage when rivals are shuffled around in a bunched finish and he has conserved all his energy; Paladin has a recent win at this trip on standard going and Rossa Ryan is an astute judge of pace. The disrupted closers, forced wide or blocked in traffic in a compressed finish, would find this shape the least sympathetic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos in Straight, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems, wide draws and scrimmaging in the straight open a gap for a hold-up horse who finds daylight at just the right moment.
scenarios.body: With 17 runners on a flat mile and multiple redistribution-tagged hold-up horses crammed into midfield, an unpredictable split in the straight could allow a horse like Barley — who has been placed at this trip on good ground in each of his last five starts — or Up The Jazz to thread through and hit the line. This is a low-probability shape because it requires both a troubled run for the prominent brigade and a perfectly-timed run from a hold-up type that may not be racing in its natural position.

watchPoints.text: Paladin's early sectionals will define this race — if Rossa Ryan bowls along unchallenged and sets a steady pace, the race will almost certainly be won by a prominent horse, so watch whether Dwindling Funds or Rajapour apply pressure in the first half-mile.

With 17 runners and six or more hold-up types competing for rear-field ground that isn't there, traffic and crowding in the straight are serious risks — Financer, Barley and Kiss Me My Love in particular may find gaps closing at critical moments.

Canvas returns from 31 days off for Scott Dixon, who has a live yard form line; horses returning from a break of that length at York on a flat mile in fast conditions need to be watched for signs of greenness or freshness in the first furlong.

Rajapour runs for the second time in six days and, while recent form includes a win, back-to-back quick turns can take the edge off a horse — watch his market move and whether cheekpieces and tongue tie again prompt a forward show early.

Financer's tongue tie and the fact she runs just six days after her last start for the volume yard of Tim Easterby (8/68 in 14 days) is worth monitoring — the yard is in form and if she can get closer to her natural hold-up position than the map suggests, her recent placed form makes her dangerous.

races.name: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Tycoon
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner, entirely uncontested at the head of affairs; trainer Kevin Philippart De Foy has a modest 14-day strike rate (2/10) but Tycoon's three placed efforts in Good ground make the conditions right, and the 7lb claim from Toby Moore softens a 142lb burden on a horse who has run creditably at this sort of trip.

runners_data.name: Likealot
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old won over 12f on Tapeta (twice placed 2nd) and has strong form at this trip, though Good to Firm is a step quicker than most of his best work; Rossa Ryan takes over with the headgear (p) re-applied, and his prominent style makes him ideally placed to exploit an uncontested front-runner's tempo.

runners_data.name: The Glen Rovers
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old who wants to race prominently but has been disappointing on Good and Standard surfaces lately (consecutive 9ths), with James Doyle the notable booking for Lucy Wadham's yard (no runners in 14 days); the one win in his last five came on Tapeta at 10f, and the step to 14f on quick ground is untested at this venue.

runners_data.name: Ashnak
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's consistent four-year-old has placed twice at this trip in Good conditions and brings a solid third last time (13f, Soft) into play; Daniel Tudhope's course knowledge is an asset, and Ashnak's prominent style means he will be right in the mix for the positions most likely to win this race shape.

runners_data.name: Wahdan
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old holds up off the pace — a style that this race shape does not particularly favour given Tycoon's anticipated controlled gallop; David Allan partners a horse whose recent form shows three consecutive 6ths and an 8th on Good ground, and the stable's 14-day strike rate (8/68) does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Caliban
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's four-year-old arrives having won two on the bounce on Tapeta at 11f, but this represents a significant surface switch to Good to Firm — his one run in this going produced a 4th over 12f; 137 days off the track is the primary concern, though a prominent-to-hold-up profile means he arrives fresh and with untapped handicap marks on turf.

runners_data.name: Chillingham
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up type with a blinkered record (hg:b) and a history of running well at distances beyond what is on offer today — three runs at 16f suggest he may lack the finishing pace for 14f on quick ground; Micky Hammond's stable is modest at 14 days (3/13) and Chillingham's recent form (three 6ths, a 9th, and a 15th) is deeply uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Damascus Steel I
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on Good just 9 days ago and Tom Eaves partners a horse who genuinely wants to race prominently — but with the front-rank positions already spoken for, he is likely to find himself racing deeper in the field than his best form warrants; his Good-ground record (5/11 in this going including two wins) is the strongest asset, and if he recovers a forward berth quickly the style mismatch is reduced.

runners_data.name: Therapist
runners_data.note: Peter Niven's six-year-old returns from 175 days off the track with an authentic stamina profile — four wins over today's trip or beyond — and his best form has come on Good ground (4W at 16-18f); naturally prominent in style, the overcrowded front section means he will likely have to settle further back than ideal, and the significant layoff is an additional risk in a field with more recent form to offer.

runners_data.name: Humble Spark
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old is a hold-up type (hg:p) whose best placed efforts have come in slower-ground races, and his recent run (6th, 12f, Good) fits the pattern of a horse who needs cut to show his best; Lauren Young's 5lb claim partially offsets the weight, but Humble Spark's profile — back of the field, needs a strong pace — is the least likely to be served by a single uncontested front-runner.

races.paceDynamic: Tycoon is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse wanting to lead in a 10-runner field, he should stride clear early and set a controlled, measured pace over this 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground — no pressure, no burn-up. Behind him, Likealot, The Glen Rovers, and Ashnak all want to press, creating a cluster of prominent types that will jostle for the handful of front-rank positions from the off, with real traffic danger likely to materialise between the 3f and 2f markers as the field converges on the home turn. Damascus Steel I and Therapist are genuine prominent-running types who have been mapped to midfield because the front-running/prominent slots are oversubscribed — they will likely find themselves racing further back than ideal, which discounts their effectiveness in scenarios that demand a handy position. This race shape — a single unhurried pace-setter, a bunched prominent group, and closers left flat-footed by a steady early clip — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in the first three, absorb any positional friction, and produce a sustained gallop from 2f out rather than a sharp finishing burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tycoon Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Tycoon dictates an unchallenged gallop and the race resolves into a test of stamina from 2f out rather than a sprint.
scenarios.body: Tycoon bowls along at a comfortable tempo, and the horses travelling in his slipstream — Likealot and Ashnak — are best placed to pounce when he comes back to the field in the final furlong; a galloping, staying test on quick ground suits this profile perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet (Likealot, The Glen Rovers, Ashnak, Caliban) interfere with each other turning for home, leaving a gap for a held-up runner.
scenarios.body: The positional friction 3-2f out checks several prominent types momentarily, allowing Caliban — fresh from a break and with two recent wins on Tapeta — or Wahdan to arrive late with momentum; this shape marginally rescues a hold-up runner but only works if the pace was genuinely strong enough to stop the prominent horses finishing.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Stands
scenarios.trigger: If Tycoon, unchallenged, sets such a slow early fraction that he simply outstays the field in the straight.
scenarios.body: Without any rival to push him, Tycoon could effectively turn this into a sprint from 2f out on his own terms, exploiting the lack of pressure; his Good-ground form is solid (three placed efforts in similar conditions) and Toby Moore's 7lb claim further assists the weight advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Make Ground
scenarios.trigger: If Damascus Steel I or Therapist manage to push forward from their expected midfield berths and reclaim a prominent position.
scenarios.body: Both horses are naturally prominent runners forced back by the congested map, and if early gaps appear they may press forward — Damascus Steel I in particular arrives on the back of a win 9 days ago and has the speed to do it; however, racing out of role means this is a low-probability shape that requires a very specific sequence of early events.

watchPoints.text: Likealot, The Glen Rovers, and Ashnak are all prominent types converging on the same two or three front positions — watch for a scrimmage approaching the home turn 3f out that could unbalance any of them and cost lengths at the critical moment.

Caliban has been off the track for 137 days and switches from Tapeta to Good to Firm turf for the first time; if he shows any ring-rustiness in the opening exchanges his prominent style will be wasted.

Damascus Steel I runs again after just 9 days and is a genuine prominent type forced back into midfield by the race shape — if he burns early energy pushing forward to reclaim his natural position, his finishing effort could be compromised.

Therapist's 175-day absence is the longest in the field; even with strong stamina form over this trip, fitness on return must be treated as a question mark and his performance should be monitored for signs he needs the run.

Tycoon's pace is the race's central variable — if Toby Moore (7lb claim, relatively inexperienced) sets too slow a tempo, the race turns into a sprint and closers are eliminated entirely; conversely, any uncharacteristic quickening early would compromise Tycoon's chance of lasting home.

races.name: Sky Bet Extra Places Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Invincible Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Fahey with a consistent record of placing at 6f on Good ground; stepping up to 7f is the key question, as all five career runs have been shorter, and he meets a competitive field from a fair mark of 80.

runners_data.name: Mr Noble
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for K. R. Burke who won over 6f at Sandown in his last outing 28 days ago; Burke's yard is firing at 10/34 in 14 days, and Mr Noble gets first run at the rail but is tagged as racing out of role if taken on — the key is whether he can boss this from the front undisturbed.

runners_data.name: Flight Control
runners_data.note: Five career starts all at 7f on Good ground with a consistent placed record; best form on this course and distance combination, and Ryan Frost's yard has a runner fit to go on a sharp 15-day turnaround — the most natural fit of any prominent type for this trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Thankfully
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who drops back to 7f after two efforts at 8f on Good ground; Burke's yard is in strong form and Mulrennan takes the ride, though the drop in trip will need to bring improvement and she has been winless in the last six outings.

runners_data.name: Return Of The Gods
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good last time and placed over 6f at Sandown — James Doyle in the saddle is a significant booking; handles this ground, is versatile enough to race prominently or track, and the combination of course-appropriate form and a top jockey makes him one of the more interesting prominent types.

runners_data.name: Bright Summer
runners_data.note: Balding yard runs him here having won over 7f at Standard (AW); his Good-ground form shows placed runs only, and in a field with this much pace he may struggle to secure a prominent berth — McDonald will need clean air.

runners_data.name: Zarvali
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good for Roger Fell and has raced exclusively on Good ground; an eight-run form record on similar conditions is a strong foundation, though his last three runs show a downward trend from his 7f win, and Fell's yard is light on recent winners.

runners_data.name: Raging Raj
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner whose record includes a 7f win on Good — Tudhope is a shrewd pilot — but with more prominent types ahead of him in this field, he is unlikely to get the lead he wants and must adapt; his style fit in a held-back position carries a discount.

runners_data.name: Toastmaster
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good for Herrington and has placed at this trip before; like stablemate Raging Raj, he races best when prominent but the field volume pushes him back — Shoemark will be working to find a position, and his 15-day turnaround suggests readiness if not ideal placement.

runners_data.name: Bleep Test
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Tim Easterby with a tongue-tie; placed at 6f on Good ground and steps up to 7f, which may suit his stamina — Easterby is placing runners prolifically (8/68 in 14 days) and Allan knows his horses, though the step up is untested.

runners_data.name: Milford Grange
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a visor fitted; multiple placed efforts on Soft at 6-7f but switches to Good today — form on similar ground is limited (2 from 6 finished in the frame) and he drops from 8f, which at least addresses stamina concerns.

runners_data.name: Forest Phoenix
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Good and has shown a tendency to fade in the finish — a significant flag over 7f; Easterby's prolific yard keeps him active on 15 days but the combination of a clear tendency to weaken and the longer trip makes this a significant test, and his redistribution to midfield from a natural prominent role compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Keep An Eye On It
runners_data.note: Unknown style who returns from a 104-day break; placed at 7f on Standard and 8f on Good, so the trip is within range, but the long absence for a small yard (Coyle/Wood at 0/8 in 14 days) makes readiness hard to assess — Hardie's local knowledge helps.

runners_data.name: Gunalt Wavelength
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has won at 7f and 6f on Good ground — two wins from five similar-going runs — and is active on a 22-day turnaround; Joanna Mason keeps the ride and the form profile shows a horse improving from the rear who could capitalise if the pace scenario sets up correctly.

runners_data.name: Dacres Cross
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Soft for Kevin Ryan but all recent form at 7f on Good shows finishes in the lower half; naturally prominent in style but unlikely to reach that position here — Ryan's yard has one winner from 21 in 14 days, and this is an uphill task from his current mark.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Noble is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with a clear track in front of him on Good to Firm ground at York, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without significant pressure from the outset. Flight Control, Invincible Boy, Return Of The Gods, Bright Summer and Zarvali all want to be prominent, meaning the early stages will see a scramble for berths, but Mr Noble's established lead habit gives him first call on the front position. Toastmaster, Raging Raj, Forest Phoenix and Dacres Cross are genuine prominent types who cannot all slot into their preferred spot given the volume of pace ahead of them, so the most likely beneficiaries of the front rank after Mr Noble are Flight Control and Return Of The Gods, who have the best evidence of racing efficiently up with the pace over this trip. With Mr Noble setting a measured, uncontested tempo, this race shape most strongly favours hold-up or late-running horses who can save ground in midfield, get a clean passage off the final bend and produce a sustained finish — prominent horses who get dragged into an early position fight risk being left flat in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Noble dictates a fair but not excessive pace and the prominent scramble burns off several rivals early, setting up a strong late run.
scenarios.body: Mr Noble's uncontested tempo through the first half keeps fractions fair but not slow, meaning those tracking in midfield to hold-up positions have enough juice left to reel in the leaders over the final two furlongs at York's long straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early battle for prominent slots is brief and settles quickly, allowing the front rank to dictate and control the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Flight Control and Return Of The Gods, both proven at 7f on Good ground, latch onto Mr Noble's pace and prove too strong for those coming from off the pace who struggle to get into the race in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runners Tire
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble is prolonged and frantic, bleeding the speed horses dry before the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A rough early race leaves the front rank vulnerable in the straight as the pace has been high enough to flatten them, handing late-moving hold-up types an unusually clear passage to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Surge
scenarios.trigger: If a moderate or stop-start pace creates a bunched mid-race and the field fans wide in the straight, rewarding those with tactical versatility.
scenarios.body: Horses redistributed from their natural front positions find themselves in unfamiliar midfield slots without rhythm, while versatile trackers with strong finishing form pick them off in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Mr Noble's ability to lead unchallenged is the single most important factor — if Flight Control or Invincible Boy pushes him hard in the opening furlong, the tempo lifts sharply and the entire race shape shifts against front-runners.

Toastmaster, Raging Raj, Forest Phoenix and Dacres Cross are all natural prominent types who cannot all get their position — watch for a chaotic opening two furlongs as several riders compete for the same ground, which may unsettle those caught in the squeeze.

Keep An Eye On It returns from 104 days off for a yard showing 0 wins from 8 in the last fortnight — if supported in the market it would indicate stable confidence, but fitness is genuinely unproven after such an absence.

Gunalt Wavelength has won twice at 6-7f on Good ground and races from hold-up — if the pace scenario unfolds as expected (fair tempo, Mr Noble leading), she is among the most naturally suited in the field to deliver a late run down York's long straight.

Forest Phoenix is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish; at 7f on Good for the first time over this trip, combined with the redistribution away from his favoured prominent role, he is worth monitoring early to see whether the rider attempts to push forward regardless — if he does, expect him to be a spent force late.
